Mixed feelings on the game.
While the game design is fine, the lack of any form of upgrades and the way skill updating works is complete missunderstanding.
Instead of getting stronger you get weaker as spells cost more and more mana, to the point combat almost stops functioning as enemies become immune to normal attacks and require spells, meanwhile you cant cast even one spell. Its easy to realise not upgrading anything is the way to go, but then ... half of the game systems become pointless.

It has other things i despise in from software game, meaning npcs dissapear as game goes on, forgot to buy something but triggered an invisible checkpoint? Good luck, your store NPC is gone for ever.
It also has invisible quest trigger failure states, while they only reward pointless items its still annoying.

Definetly a great metroidvania, easily the most chill and relaxing one i've ever played, which is kind of weird for the genre it is.
The combat may be a bit boring at the start but the bosses do improve throughout the game and are pretty good, sure they may not be on the level of the greats like hollow knight, but they are good enough (and the boss rush mode is decent too).
The exploring aspect of the game is also good, with good backtracking, with it being not too boring, and opening new paths and shortcuts for the whole playthrough.
Overall a good, chill metroidvania, which doesn't take itself too seriously but has an interesting and unique mechanic for the map (that being the islands connecting to each other to unlock new paths).

I didn't get the first game. I thought it was pretty mid. Now something clicked, I enjoyed time with this standalone DLC or sequel or whatever a lot more than the original.

Not everything is great. The environment can get repetitive quite quickly. The game is also a little shorter than the prequel (easy 100%).

Besides that, it's really just fun. I turned my brain off and just started shooting the bad guys. It was just plain old fun, nothing fancy, just fun. In this game, they introduce more enemy variety, which is a huge plus. 

I really didn't focus on the story, so I can't give any in-depth analysis of the topic, but it was fine and better than the first game, in my opinion. 

That's all I had to say on the topic. Have fun!

10 hours in and already loving it.

I’ve played around 10 hours so far and beaten roughly 9-10 bosses. Some fights definitely feel a little unfair at times, especially when you’re getting destroyed over and over again, but that’s also what makes finally beating them so satisfying.

The combat feels great, the bosses are challenging, and every victory actually feels earned rather than handed to you. There are definitely moments where I question my life choices, but when you finally figure out the boss and take it down… that feeling is worth it.

Really enjoying the game so far. Definitely recommend it if you like challenging boss fights  worth it bro you can buy (:
